Yeah, I can see how that might be a bit weird to tell people.

Definitely kinks and sexuality. In person, people expect you to answer questions right away. Online, I have time to formulate a response, look it over to make sure it makes sense, and to see if it could be misinterpreted very easily. People make assumptions about what you like, why you like it, and what it says about you. There's also a creep factor to talking about these things in person. You never know who you're going to gross out, who's going to take talking about sexuality as an invitation to flirt with you, and when anonymity's gone, people gossip and inevitably someone has to be a shithead about your personal, private enjoyments. If someone on the internet is a shithead, I can easily ignore them; if someone IRL is a shithead, I probably have to deal with them on a regular basis, and they know people I know.

I'm also pretty private about most of my opinions, about religion (my lack thereof), sexual orientation, relationships, etc. Basically, I don't like to provide openers to conversations unless I think they're worth my time to deal with. I may find a topic interesting, but that doesn't mean I want to discuss it with any particular person. It's not their business, and if talking about a topic with a person is likely to only provide me frustration and no growth on either end, it is worse than wasted time.
